season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.description: cfb.bowl_selection_state flags eligibility at six raw wins; the NCAA rule that only one win over an FCS opponent counts, the 5-7 APR fallback order and 2026 waivers are not verified here and change which bubble teams are eligible for KXNCAAFBOWLGAME.
season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.what_would_resolve: The 2026 NCAA postseason bowl-eligibility bylaw text and the APR fallback list procedure.
season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.classification_rationale: Checked: only one win over an FCS opponent (meeting the scholarship requirement) counts toward six, and 5-7 teams fill unfilled slots in APR order. cfb.bowl_selection_state counts raw wins >=6 and has no FCS-opponent win cap or APR source, so the definition is demonstrably wrong and needs new raw inputs (opponent division per win, APR scores).
season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.catalog_action: Amend cfb.bowl_selection_state: count at most one qualifying FCS win, add an opponent-division flag per game and an NCAA APR score source for the 5-7 fallback order, citing the current NCAA postseason bylaw and any 2026 waiver.

season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.description: The CFP committee resume model (cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model) is re-derived here and as cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features in the polls archetype, a duplication risk: a change to one would not propagate to the other.
season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.what_would_resolve: Choose one canonical committee-behaviour input in the catalog and alias the other.
season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.classification_rationale: cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model (season_futures) and cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features (polls_and_cfp_rankings) define the same committee rank model with different feature lists; two diverging definitions of one input is a catalog defect fixed by authoring, not data.
season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.catalog_action: Make cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features the canonical committee rank input (or the reverse), merge feature lists, and alias the other id in the season_futures and unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings records.

touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.description: The registered archetype is touchdown scorer markets (anytime and first player) but the ledger shows no live named-player touchdown series, only team and game counts; if player series are listed later the player-role inputs (td_rates, depth_chart, player_usage) become primary and are currently untestable.
touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.what_would_resolve: Re-check the live Kalshi series list for named-player touchdown markets and re-key the archetype into player and team-count parts.
touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.classification_rationale: The archetype is keyed to anytime/first player TD markets, but the ledger's live series are team and game TD counts; player-role inputs (td_rates, depth_chart, player_usage) are primary for absent series. That is a series/archetype mapping defect in the records.
touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.catalog_action: Re-check live Kalshi CFB TD series, re-key touchdown_scorer to the live team/game TD-count series (td_count_dispersion, td_per_scoring_trip, dst_td_propensity primary) and mark the player part dormant with player inputs secondary.

unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.description: After the reconciliation team stat counts are split between game_stat_props (yards, touchdowns, rushing attempts) and this archetype (sacks, interceptions, turnovers, field goals, two-point conversions, delays), and cfb.opp_dropback_volume overlaps cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts and cfb.state_dependent_pace used there.
unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.what_would_resolve: Alias cfb.opp_dropback_volume to the game_stat_props dropback input in the catalog, or document why the defensive view needs a separate definition.
unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.classification_rationale: cfb.opp_dropback_volume's own definition says it measures the same quantity as cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts plus cfb.state_dependent_pace and should be aliased; two definitions of one input across split archetypes is an unresolved catalog duplication.
unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.catalog_action: Alias cfb.opp_dropback_volume to cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts (opponent view) in the team_event_counting_specials and season_stat_leader records, or document a distinct defensive-view definition.
